## How to read the declared files

This project has two codelines, each with its own root:

- mocka — /home/bradleyjerome/projects/mock3/mock-a
- mockb — /home/bradleyjerome/projects/mock3/mock-b

Declared file paths are relative to the root of the codeline that owns them, not to any shared parent. A path such as src/fares.ts or test/fares.test.ts resolves under mocka; src/schedule.ts or test/schedule.test.ts resolves under mockb. The two codelines carry the same declared dependencies (typescript, vitest) and use the same src/ and test/ layout, so a bare relative path is ambiguous until you pair it with its codeline. Never assume a file in one codeline has a counterpart in the other, and never let evidence gathered in mocka stand in for evidence about mockb or the reverse.

Both tickets in this project are narrow logic corrections in TypeScript pure functions with existing vitest coverage — an off-by-one or boundary-comparison class of defect. Two traps follow from that, and a specification that ignores them will be wrong in a way the tests do not catch:

- Boundary conditions are the whole story here. When you state expected behaviour, state it at the exact boundary value and on both sides of it, not as a general rule. "Riders aged exactly 65" and "the final stop" are the cases under specification; a spec that only describes the interior of the range specifies nothing.
- The existing vitest suites may already pass while the defect is live, because the boundary case is untested rather than mis-tested. Do not infer from a green suite that behaviour is correct, and do not describe current behaviour from test names alone.
